title: HILIC-MS/MS Data Acquisition and Processing of Label-Free GAG Disaccharides
author: H Davies-Strickleton
materials: Initial review of results and acceptance criteria

In the LC-MS software, create the LC-MS acquisition method parameters for the analysis of HS disaccharides Create acquisition methods using the LC-MS conditions detailed here. Note: exact LC conditions may need to be optimised for isomer separation (e.g. via test injections as described later). This is based on the observation that new HILIC-Z columns, and columns that had been stored, required LC gradients to be adjusted by up to +/- 5% B. MS settings (CE and/or DP) can also be adjusted to ensure satisfactory fragmentation.

In the LC-MS software, create the LC-MS acquisition method parameters for the analysis of CS/DS/HA disaccharides Create acquisition methods using the LC-MS conditions detailed here. Note: exact LC conditions may need to be optimised for isomer separation (e.g. via test injections as described later). This is based on the observation that new HILIC-Z columns, and columns that had been stored, required LC gradients to be adjusted by up to +/- 5% B. MS settings (CE and/or DP) can also be adjusted to ensure satisfactory fragmentation.

steps.title: Prepare 250 mM Ammonium Acetate Stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 19.27 g ammonium acetate (VWR #84885.180, MW = 77.08 g·mol⁻¹) into a 1 L Duran bottle, add ddH₂O to a final volume of 1 L, mix well, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 year. Use V = m/(C·MW) to adjust volumes if a different mass is weighed (e.g., 20 g → 1.037 L).

steps.title: Make Mobile Phase A (25 mM)
steps.instruction: Combine 9 parts water with 1 part 250 mM ammonium acetate stock (1:10 dilution) to obtain 25 mM ammonium acetate in water. Example for 500 mL: add 450 mL ddH₂O and 50 mL stock, mix, and use within 1 month.

steps.title: Make Mobile Phase B (25 mM, 85% ACN)
steps.instruction: Combine 85 parts LC‑MS grade acetonitrile, 10 parts 250 mM ammonium acetate stock (1:10 dilution), and 5 parts water (total 100 parts) to give 25 mM ammonium acetate in 85 % ACN. Example for 1 L: 850 mL ACN, 100 mL stock, 50 mL water, mix, let reach room temperature, and store up to 3 months.

steps.title: Prepare Wash Solvent (80% ACN)
steps.instruction: Mix 4 parts LC‑MS grade acetonitrile with 1 part water (total 5 parts). Example for 300 mL: 240 mL ACN, 60 mL water, mix, let reach room temperature, and store up to 3 months.

steps.title: Prepare Storage Buffer (50% ACN, 5 mM)
steps.instruction: Combine 25 parts acetonitrile, 24 parts water, and 1 part 250 mM ammonium acetate stock (1:50 dilution) to give 5 mM ammonium acetate in 50 % ACN. Example for 100 mL: 50 mL ACN, 48 mL water, 2 mL stock, mix, let reach room temperature, and store up to 3 months.

steps.title: Install HILIC‑Z Column and Guard
steps.instruction: Mount the P120 HILIC‑Z column (2.1 × 150 mm, 2.7 µm, Agilent #673775‑924) and the InfinityLab Poroshell 120 HILIC Guard (Agilent #821725‑947) in the LC system according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Degas and Purge Solvents Through LC System
steps.instruction: Degas Mobile Phase A, Mobile Phase B, and Wash solvent (step #2‑#4) and then purge the LC system with these solvents to remove dissolved gases.

steps.title: Equilibrate Column with Starting Gradient
steps.instruction: Run the initial gradient (starting conditions) to equilibrate the column. For heparan sulfate (HS) analysis continue to step 9; for chondroitin‑/dermatan‑sulfate/HA (CS/DS/HA) continue to step 11.

steps.title: Run Test Injections of Standard
steps.instruction: Inject an equimolar disaccharide standard at a high concentration (e.g., 5000 nM) to test chromatographic separation and MS/MS fragmentation. Adjust LC‑MS/MS settings until isomer separation and satisfactory fragmentation are achieved.

steps.title: Prepare Injection Vials and Autosampler
steps.instruction: Prepare vials containing: (i) Blank Diluent (no analyte), (ii) Blank Internal Standard (IS only), (iii) Equimolar Disaccharide Standard at 50 nM, (iv) Positive Control Sample, (v) Test Samples, and optionally (vi) Linearity Standards at 5, 500, and 5000 nM. Place all vials in the autosampler at least 90 min before injection so they equilibrate to 5 °C. Use separate vials for repeat injections to avoid signal depletion.

steps.title: Perform Batch Injections with LC‑MS/MS Settings
steps.instruction: Inject each vial (5 µL injection volume) using the appropriate LC gradient and MS/MS method for the GAG type.

substeps.instruction: Set LC cooler to 5 °C and oven to 50 °C; flow rate 0.25 mL·min⁻¹.

HS MS/MS (method 30 min): source OptiFlow 50‑200 µL Micro/MicroCal, curtain gas 30, CAD gas 7, ion source gas 1 50 psi, gas 2 70 psi, temperature 250 °C, scan type MRMhr, polarity negative, spray voltage ‑4500 V. TOF‑MS/MS transitions as listed for HD001‑HD008 and IS.
CS/DS/HA MS/MS (method 35 min): same source settings, TOF‑MS/MS transitions as listed for HA02, CD001‑CD008 and IS.
Collect data for each injection; repeat injections from fresh vials if needed.

steps.title: Store Column and Guard in Storage Buffer
steps.instruction: After completing all batches, place the HILIC‑Z column and guard column in the prepared Storage Buffer (50 % ACN, 5 mM ammonium acetate) for storage.

steps.title: Integrate Peaks and Calculate Area Ratios
steps.instruction: Using SCIEX OS v3.0, integrate peak areas with the peak‑to‑peak S/N algorithm; accept only peaks with S/N ≥ 3. Generate extracted ion chromatograms for the IS (m/z 552.0336 → 472.0781) and for each disaccharide (summed transitions as listed). Compute each disaccharide’s peak‑area ratio = (disaccharide area) / (IS area). Visually inspect all integrations.

steps.title: Semi‑Quantify Disaccharides Using Single‑Point Calibration
steps.instruction: Use the 50 nM Equimolar Disaccharide Standard as a single‑point calibrant (represents 20 pmol injected). For each disaccharide: Amount (pmol) = (Peak‑area ratio sample / Peak‑area ratio 50 nM standard) × 20 pmol.

steps.title: Export Ratios and Compute Total GAG Amounts
steps.instruction: Export all disaccharide peak‑area ratios to Excel, then calculate the absolute amount (pmol) for each disaccharide using the formula above. Sum the amounts of all HS disaccharides to obtain total HS (pmol); sum all CS/DS disaccharides for total CS/DS; for HA the single HA02 amount equals total HA.

steps.title: Calculate Disaccharide Composition Percentages
steps.instruction: For each sample, compute % composition = (disaccharide amount / total GAG amount) × 100 %. Perform this for HS and for CS/DS separately.

steps.title: Review Positive Control Consistency
steps.instruction: Compare the % composition of the Positive Control Sample to previously analysed controls of the same type; values should be consistent.

steps.title: Optional: Assess Linearity of Standards
steps.instruction: If linearity standards (5, 500, 5000 nM) were injected, fit peak‑area ratios versus concentration. Require at least three concentrations (including 50 nM) with r² ≥ 0.9 and S/N ≥ 3 for each disaccharide.
